application.name: Clarity Studio
application.description: AI-powered legacy data conversion platform. Connects to SQL/Snowflake databases, discovers schema, maps source columns to XML target structure, generates XML output, and provides AI dashboards, reporting, and PS Co-worker agent capabilities.

tech_stack.frontend: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + MUI v5 + TanStack Query v5 + Recharts
tech_stack.backend: Python FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + SQL Server (DESKTOP-G01PH8C\SQLEXPRESS / ConversionAgent DB)
tech_stack.ai: OpenAI GPT-4o-mini (mapping, SQL generation, dashboards, chat)
tech_stack.auth: Session-based (Zustand store), demo credentials: admin / clarity2024

user_journey: 1. Login → 2. Select/Create Project → 3. Add Data Connection → 4. Collect Schema (Admin) → 5. Upload XML Template (Target tab) → 6. Generate Query + Mapping (Mapping tab) → 7. Generate All XML (Output tab) → 8. Validate XML (Validation tab) → 9. Explore Data (My Dashboards) → 10. Automate (PS Support + API Collection)

login.flow: Enter credentials → set user in global store → redirect to /projects
actions: login with username + password

projects.purpose: Create and select a project workspace. All data (connections, templates, mappings, dashboards) is scoped to the active project.
projects.flow: View project cards → click a project to select it → redirect to /dashboard
actions: create project
edit project name/description
delete project
select active project

dashboard.purpose: Executive overview of the conversion pipeline. Shows 12 pipeline stages with counts, recent activity feed, and charts.
dashboard.guard: must be logged in + project selected

conversion.purpose: Core 5-tab data conversion engine. Takes source data (DB or file) through XML template mapping to produce XML output.
conversion.guard: must be logged in + project selected

source.purpose: Connect to a SQL or Snowflake data source, test the connection, and preview data
actions: test connection
preview data (first 50 rows)
save connection
load saved connection

api.POST /api/connections/{id}/run: run custom SQL using stored credentials

target.purpose: Upload an XML template that defines the output structure. Leaf elements/attributes become mapping targets. Previously saved templates and formula rules are auto-loaded when a connection is selected.
actions: Select connection → auto-loads saved template + formula rules from DB
Drop/upload new XML file → parses tree and paths in browser
Save Template → POST /api/target-formulas/process (saves XML + extracts formula rules)
Clear → reset the upload area

xml_conventions.each attribute: e.g. each='Employee' → iterates over rows from that table

target.auto_load_on_connection_select: GET /api/target-formulas/{connId}/template + GET /api/target-formulas?conn_id= are called automatically when connection changes

api.POST /api/target-formulas/process: save XML template + extract formula rules (requires conn_id)
api.GET /api/target-formulas?conn_id=: list saved formula rules for connection
api.GET /api/target-formulas/{connId}/templa: get saved raw XML template content for a connection

mapping.purpose: Map source database columns to target XML paths. AI generates the SQL query and field-to-field mapping using schema embeddings. Saved mappings and SQL are auto-loaded when a connection is selected.
actions: Select connection → auto-loads saved mapping rows + generated SQL + identifier column from DB
Generate Query (AI) — builds JOIN-aware SQL using BFS over FK graph + LLM refinement → returns {query_sql, identifier_column, identifier_table}
Preview Data — runs saved generated query (TOP 10) and shows results table
Generate Mapping (AI) — cosine similarity between target path embeddings and source column embeddings
Set Identifier Column — auto-populated from Generate Query response; one XML file generated per unique value
Edit mapping rows manually (add/delete/update)
Save Mapping → saves rows + identifier_column to DB
mapping.prerequisite: Admin tab 'Collect Schema' + 'Generate Embeddings' must be run first for AI mapping
mapping.auto_load_on_connection_select: GET /api/mapping/{connId} + GET /api/mapping/{connId}/query are called automatically. State is cleared then repopulated when connection changes.

api.POST /api/mapping/generate/query: AI-generate SQL query → returns {query_sql, identifier_column, identifier_table}
api.POST /api/mapping/generate/rows: AI-generate mapping rows using embeddings → returns {rows:[]}
api.GET /api/mapping/{connId}: load saved mapping rows + identifier_column + identifier_table
api.GET /api/mapping/{connId}/query: load saved generated SQL → returns {query_sql, identifier_column, identifier_table}
api.GET /api/mapping/{connId}/preview: preview generated SQL (TOP 10 rows) → returns {columns, rows, row_count}

output.purpose: Generate XML output per identifier value. Applies mapping field substitution and iteration. Previously generated XMLs are shown in a list and can be re-loaded.
output.layout: Three panels: Generated XMLs list (left) | XML Preview (center) | API Configuration (right)
output.toolbar_order: Connection → Generate All XML button → count chip → Preview Single Identifier dropdown
actions: Select connection → auto-loads list of already-generated XMLs
Generate All XML → runs SQL grouped by identifier_column → one XML per unique value → returns {count}
Preview Single Identifier dropdown → appears after identifier-values loaded → selecting one generates + displays XML for that record
Click item in Generated XMLs list → loads stored XML content into preview panel
Copy XML to clipboard
Download XML as file
Send to API — configurable endpoint URL, HTTP method, content-type, bearer token, extra headers

xml_generation_logic.generate_all: Runs full SQL query, groups rows by identifier_column value, generates one XML per group
xml_generation_logic.generate_one: Filters SQL by WHERE [identifier_column] = '{value}', generates XML for matching rows
xml_generation_logic.filter_column: Uses mapping.identifier_column — NOT a virtual __identifier__ alias

api.GET /api/mapping/{connId}/identifier-val: get distinct identifier values → returns {identifier_column, values:[]}
api.POST /api/mapping/{connId}/generate-xml: generate XML for one identifier value → filters SQL by identifier_column → returns {xml, identifier_value, rows_used, saved_id}
api.POST /api/mapping/{connId}/generate-all-: batch generate XML for all identifier values → groups by identifier_column → returns {count}
api.GET /api/mapping/{connId}/generated-xml: list already-generated XML records → returns [{id, identifier_value, generated_at}]
api.GET /api/mapping/{connId}/generated-xml/: load stored XML content → returns {id, identifier_value, xml_content}

validation.purpose: Define per-path validation rules, generate XSD schema, and validate generated XML output against those rules. Saved rules are auto-loaded when a connection is selected.
actions: Select connection → auto-loads saved validation rules from DB
Import Paths from Template — calls GET /api/target-formulas?conn_id= to pre-fill rule rows with XML paths
Edit rules: xml_path, is_required, data_type, min/max_length, pattern, enumeration, min/max_value
Add Rule manually
Save Rules → replaces all rules for the connection
Generate XSD → builds XSD from rules + saved XML template structure → display + download
Run Validation → validates every GeneratedXml record against saved rules → shows pass/fail per identifier
validation.rule_field_mapping: Frontend uses 'xml_path' field name; DB stores as 'target_path'
validation.auto_load_on_connection_select: GET /api/validation/{connId} is called automatically when connection changes

api.GET /api/validation/{connId}: list validation rules for connection → returns [{id, conn_id, xml_path, is_required, data_type, ...}]
api.POST /api/validation/{connId}/save: replace all rules — body: {rules: [{xml_path, is_required, data_type, ...}]}
api.POST /api/validation/{connId}/generate-x: generate XSD from rules + XML template → returns {xsd, rule_count}
api.POST /api/validation/{connId}/run: validate all GeneratedXml records → returns {valid, total, failed, errors:[{identifier, path, message}]}

my_dashboards.purpose: AI-powered dynamic dashboard builder. Describe what you want in plain English or provide a SQL query, and AI generates a full interactive dashboard with charts, KPIs, and tables.
my_dashboards.guard: must be logged in + project selected

ai_intent.description: User types a natural language intent (e.g. 'Show employee performance by department'). AI uses the DB schema to write all widget SQLs and layout.

sql_query.description: User writes one master SQL query. AI analyzes the result columns + sample rows and decides which charts/KPIs to generate.

widget_types.kpi: Single big number. SQL returns one row, one numeric column.
widget_types.bar: Bar chart. SQL returns text column (xField) + numeric column (yField).
widget_types.line: Area/line chart. Same fields as bar.
widget_types.pie: Pie chart. SQL returns text column (labelField) + numeric column (valueField).
widget_types.doughnut: Doughnut chart. Same as pie with inner hole.
widget_types.table: Data table. SQL returns any columns.

layout.collision_resolver: Frontend fixLayout() greedy algorithm pushes overlapping widgets down

actions: save new (POST)
update existing (PUT — update-or-create via activeSaved state)
load from list
delete
saved_dashboards.persistence: Stored in conversion_dashboard_configs table as config_json (DashboardConfigSchema) + debug_json (AI metadata)

my_dashboards.ai_debug_panel: View full AI prompts, schema used, query context, widget SQLs. Regenerate individual widgets with refinement instructions.

api.POST /api/dashboards/generate: AI generate from intent → returns {config, debug}
api.POST /api/dashboards/generate-from-sql: AI generate from SQL result columns + sample rows → returns {config, debug}
api.POST /api/dashboards/widget/regenerate: refine one widget with new instructions → returns {widget}

ps_support.purpose: Professional services hub. AI chat for data queries, workflow automation, connection-scoped API management, and email settings.
ps_support.guard: must be logged in + project selected

ai_chat.purpose: Chat with AI assistant about your data. AI can look up schema, generate SQL, execute SQL, call APIs from the collection, preview emails, and generate reports.
ai_chat.connection_scoped: Conversations are filtered by selected connection. Conversation list only shows conversations for the currently selected connection (GET /api/ps/conversations?conn_id=).
ai_chat.tool_loop: Agent loop: AI calls tools (lookup_schema, generate_sql, execute_sql, list_api_endpoints, execute_api, execute_api_bulk, preview_email, generate_report), feeds results back to LLM, repeats up to 10 rounds.
ai_chat.api_execution_flow: 1. User requests data modification → 2. AI calls list_api_endpoints (returns id, name, description, method, url, body_template, required_fields) → 3. AI reads required_fields to know which SQL columns to fetch → 4. AI generates SQL to SELECT those columns → 5. AI calls execute_api_bulk(api_id, sql, payload_template) → one approval covers all records
ai_chat.approval_mechanism: execute_api and execute_api_bulk always require explicit user approval via approval card UI. execute_sql write ops (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) also require approval.

api.POST /api/ps/chat: streaming SSE: send message, returns tool_start / tool_done / text / approval_request / done events

workflows.purpose: Create and schedule automated workflows (sequences of SQL/API/email steps).

email_settings.purpose: Configure SMTP for AI to send emails as workflow actions.

api_collection.purpose: Full management page for REST API definitions used by the PS AI agent. Two-panel layout: left list with connection filter, right editor form.
api_collection.guard: must be logged in + project selected
api_collection.connection_scoped: Each API entry has an optional conn_id. The page header has a connection filter dropdown. PS Chat only calls APIs matching the active conversation's conn_id.

fields_per_entry.name: Human-readable name. AI reads this to identify the right API.
fields_per_entry.description: What this API does. AI reads this to decide when to call it.
fields_per_entry.method: HTTP method: GET / POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE
fields_per_entry.body_template: JSON body with {{field_name}} placeholders — filled by execute_api engine from SQL row data
fields_per_entry.required_fields: JSON array of field names the API needs (e.g. ["emp_id","deptno"]). AI uses this to know which columns to SELECT before building the payload.
fields_per_entry.auth_value: Token or user:password — stored Fernet-encrypted, never returned in API responses
fields_per_entry.conn_id: Optional — restricts this API entry to a specific data connection

api_collection.test_panel: Inline HTTP test sender — sends actual request and shows status + response body

api.GET /api/ps/api-collection?conn_id=: list API entries (filtered by connection if provided)

admin.purpose: Database schema discovery, embedding generation, and AI context management. Must be run before AI mapping works.
admin.guard: must be logged in + project selected
prerequisite_for: AI SQL generation in PS Chat

schema_discovery.purpose: Connect to the source DB and collect all tables, columns, data types, FK relationships, and sample rows.
schema_discovery.action: Click 'Collect Schema' → streams progress via SSE

api.GET /api/admin/discover/{connId}: SSE stream of schema discovery progress

embeddings.purpose: Generate OpenAI embeddings for all discovered column names. Used for semantic column matching in AI mapping.

catalog_viewer.purpose: Browse discovered tables, columns, relationships, and sample data.

query_context.purpose: Store custom instructions/context injected into ALL AI prompts (dashboards, mapping, reports, PS chat). Can be global (conn_id = NULL) or per-connection.
query_context.example: Do not use ORDER BY. Always filter active records only. Use department codes not names.
query_context.scope: global (conn_id = NULL) rows + connection-specific rows are both appended to every AI prompt

query_examples.purpose: Store example question→SQL pairs to help AI generate better queries (few-shot examples).

data_quality.purpose: View table/column/FK statistics for the discovered schema.

Project.description: Top-level workspace. All data is scoped to a project.

SourceConnection.description: Saved DB connection (SQL or Snowflake). Credentials are Fernet-encrypted at rest.
SourceConnection.security: Passwords never returned in API responses. Always encrypted with Fernet.

XmlTemplate.description: Uploaded XML file content saved per connection.

TargetFormulaRule.description: One extracted XML leaf path + its formula type and optional default value.

Mapping.description: Mapping header for a connection — links identifier column and contains field rows.

MappingRow.description: One source column → target XML path mapping entry.

GeneratedQuery.description: AI-generated SQL query for a connection. Stored separately from mapping rows.

GeneratedXml.description: Generated XML output stored per identifier value. Has validation_status after running validation.

CatalogColumn.description: Discovered schema column (from Admin → Collect Schema).

CatalogSample.description: Up to 3 sample rows per table (for AI context).

ColumnEmbedding.description: OpenAI embedding vector for a column name (used for semantic matching in AI mapping).

DashboardConfig.description: Saved AI-generated dashboard. config_json is DashboardConfigSchema JSON. debug_json has AI prompt metadata.

QueryContext.description: Custom AI instructions injected into all AI prompts. conn_id = NULL means global (applies to all connections).

PsConversation.description: AI chat conversation thread in PS Support. Scoped to a connection.

PsApiCollection.description: Predefined REST API endpoint the PS AI agent can call. Optionally scoped to a connection.
notes: required_fields: JSON array of field names AI must fetch via SQL before building payload (e.g. ["emp_id","deptno"])
body_template: JSON with {{field_name}} placeholders — auto-filled per row by execute_api_bulk engine
auth_value_enc: stored Fernet-encrypted, never returned in API responses

PsWorkflow.schedule: PsWorkflowSchedule row (type: manual | interval | daily | weekly)

ValidationRule.description: XSD-style validation rule for a target XML path. DB column is target_path; frontend field is xml_path.

steps: 1. User selects connection + types natural language intent
2. POST /api/dashboards/generate
3. Backend fetches schema (CatalogColumn + CatalogRelation) for the connection
4. Backend fetches Query Context (global + connection-specific) from QueryContext table
5. Builds prompt: intent + schema + relationships + query context
6. Calls OpenAI GPT-4o-mini → returns DashboardConfigSchema JSON
7. Frontend renders widget grid using fixLayout() collision resolver
8. Each widget fetches its own data via POST /api/connections/{id}/run

widgets.type: kpi | bar | line | pie | doughnut | table
widgets.title: string

steps: 1. User writes a master SQL query + optional visualization hint
2. Frontend runs the SQL: POST /api/connections/{id}/run
3. Takes column names + first 10 rows as sample
4. POST /api/dashboards/generate-from-sql with {sql, columns, sample_rows, intent}
5. Backend fetches Query Context and appends to prompt
6. AI decides which charts best represent the data
7. Each widget SQL is a variation of the user's master SQL (aggregated/sliced)
1. Generate Query: BFS traversal of FK graph builds JOIN SQL → LLM refines it → returns {query_sql, identifier_column, identifier_table}
2. identifier_column is auto-populated in the Identifier Column field in the Mapping tab UI
3. Preview Data: runs saved SQL TOP 10 → shows results table in UI
4. Generate Mapping: cosine similarity between target XML path embeddings and source column embeddings
5. High confidence (≥80%) = auto-mapped, Medium (≥55%) = suggested, Low = manual
6. Save Mapping → stores rows + identifier_column in DB for later retrieval
ai_mapping.auto_load: When connection is selected, both mapping rows and generated SQL are loaded from DB automatically (GET /api/mapping/{connId} + GET /api/mapping/{connId}/query)

steps: 1. POST /api/mapping/{connId}/generate-all-xml
2. Runs full SQL query directly against the data source
3. Groups rows by mapping.identifier_column value (NOT by __identifier__ — that alias doesn't exist)
4. Falls back to first column if identifier_column is NULL
5. For each group: substitutes {ColumnName} placeholders in XML template
6. Saves one GeneratedXml record per identifier value
7. Returns {count: N}
1. POST /api/mapping/{connId}/generate-xml with {identifier_value}
2. Wraps SQL in subquery: SELECT * FROM ({sql}) AS _src WHERE [identifier_column] = '{value}'
3. identifier_column comes from mapping.identifier_column (auto-detected from first column if NULL)
4. Generates XML from matching rows
5. Saves/updates the GeneratedXml record
6. Returns {xml, identifier_value, rows_used, saved_id}

ps_chat_api_execution.purpose: When user asks AI to modify data (create/update/fix records), AI uses the API Collection instead of writing SQL directly.
steps: 1. User sends chat message: 'Create policy for last 5 employees in dept 10'
2. AI calls list_api_endpoints → gets [{id, name, description, method, url, body_template, required_fields}]
3. AI reads required_fields (e.g. ['emp_id','deptno']) to know what data to fetch
4. AI generates SQL: SELECT TOP 5 EMPNO as emp_id, DEPTNO as deptno FROM EMP WHERE DEPTNO=10
5. For MULTIPLE records: AI calls execute_api_bulk(api_id, sql, payload_template={emp_id: EMPNO, deptno: DEPTNO})
6. Backend fetches rows, fills body_template placeholders per row, calls API once per record
7. User sees approval card: count + sample payload. One approval covers all records.
8. AI returns summary: N succeeded, M failed
ps_chat_api_execution.for_single_records: AI calls execute_api(api_id, payload) with explicit field values. Requires separate approval per call.

tool_list.lookup_schema: Search schema catalog for relevant tables/columns by keyword
tool_list.generate_sql: Generate SELECT SQL from natural language question
tool_list.execute_sql: Execute SQL query against the connected data source
tool_list.list_api_endpoints: List all APIs in the collection for the active connection → includes body_template + required_fields
tool_list.execute_api: Call one API with an explicit payload (always requires user approval)
tool_list.execute_api_bulk: Run SQL → for each row call the same API (one approval covers all)
tool_list.preview_email: Render an email preview (never actually sends)
tool_list.generate_report: Format query results as a markdown report

query_context_injection.description: Any text saved in Admin → Query Context is automatically appended to AI prompts across all AI features.
query_context_injection.scope: global (NULL conn_id) rows + connection-specific rows are both appended

security: Full datasets never sent to browser — only status/counts/errors
Passwords and API tokens always Fernet-encrypted at rest, never returned in API responses
fetch_all_data() is internal only — never exposed as HTTP endpoint
sql_server_quirks: Use TOP N not LIMIT N for row limiting
ORDER BY not allowed in subqueries without TOP/OFFSET — stripped by _wrap_query()
Named instances (host contains \) must NOT have port appended in connection string
Column names with spaces or special chars must be wrapped in [brackets]
routing_rules: All API routers must be registered via include_router BEFORE the SPA catch-all route (/{full_path:path})
The SPA catch-all is inside 'if _STATIC_DIR.exists()' block — any route defined after this block is unreachable
target_formulas router is registered as a proper router (not inline in main.py) to avoid catch-all shadowing
connection_scoping: PS Conversations filtered by conn_id — GET /api/ps/conversations?conn_id= returns only that connection's threads
API Collection entries have optional conn_id — GET /api/ps/api-collection?conn_id= filters if provided
AI Chat list_api_endpoints tool returns only APIs matching the active conversation's conn_id
Validation rules, mappings, templates all scoped to conn_id

field_name_map.identifier_values_response: returns {identifier_column, values:[]} — frontend extracts .values for the dropdown
field_name_map.validation_rule_path_field: frontend uses 'xml_path'; DB column is 'target_path' — router maps between them

auto_load_patterns.target_tab: On connection select: load template (GET /api/target-formulas/{connId}/template) + rules (GET /api/target-formulas?conn_id=)
auto_load_patterns.mapping_tab: On connection select: clear rows/sql/identifierCol, then load mapping (GET /api/mapping/{connId}) + query (GET /api/mapping/{connId}/query)
auto_load_patterns.validation_tab: On connection select: clear rules, then load (GET /api/validation/{connId})
auto_load_patterns.output_tab: On connection select: load generated XML list (GET /api/mapping/{connId}/generated-xml) + identifier values

key_rules_and_constraints.xml_generation_filter: generate_xml_for_identifier and generate_all_xml both use mapping.identifier_column (not __identifier__ alias) to filter/group rows
key_rules_and_constraints.connection_names: Must be unique per project (enforced by 409 on duplicate name)
key_rules_and_constraints.xml_template_prerequisite: Must be saved (with connection selected) before mapping can be generated
key_rules_and_constraints.schema_collection_prerequisite: Must run 'Collect Schema' in Admin before AI mapping or dashboard generation works
key_rules_and_constraints.dashboard_save: Update-or-create pattern: activeSaved state determines POST vs PUT — subsequent saves update the same record
